name: Ashes of the Ivory Court
description: Succession intrigue in a city-state whose throne has just burned. Three factions, secrets as currency, and assassins as punctuation. Social-first play where violence is rare and always costs something.
author: BMO VTT
toneInstructions: Write like a tense drawing-room drama: most scenes are conversations, and the real weapons are secrets, favors, and reputation. Keep prose elegant and controlled; let subtext do the work, and give NPCs distinct verbal tics. Track who owes whom. Violence should be rare, sudden, and consequential — an assassination reshapes the board, it doesn't reset it. Reward players who listen, remember, and trade information cleverly. End scenes on a revealed secret or a debt incurred, and never tell the players what a character 'really' means — show it and let them infer.

openingScene.title: The Throne Still Smoking
openingScene.readAloud: The Ivory Court earns its name no longer. Three nights ago the throne-hall burned, the old Sovereign with it, and the city of Ashglance woke to a crown without a head and a hundred heads that want it. Now you stand in the Hall of Petitions, where the smoke-stain still climbs one marble wall, and three delegations pretend not to watch each other across the floor: the Sovereign's grieving daughter in mourning grey, the Lord Chancellor in unburnt finery, and the masked envoy of the Guilds. A herald clears her throat. 'The succession,' she announces, 'will be decided by the Court within the fortnight.' Quieter, to you alone, a steward murmurs: 'Whoever you came here serving — they've already lied to you about why.'
openingScene.dmNotes: All three claimants have a real claim and a real crime. The steward (Ysolde, NPC) is the party's way in and the truest reading of the board. The fire was not an accident; who set it is the central secret. Keep early scenes talky and let the party pick a patron — or play all three.

lore.title: The Ivory Court
lore.content: The ruling council of the city-state of Ashglance, named for its pale marble hall — now smoke-stained after the throne-fire that killed the Sovereign.

lore.title: The Throne-Fire
lore.content: The blaze that killed the Sovereign three nights ago. Ruled an accident by the Chancellor; everyone with sense suspects otherwise.

lore.title: Three Claims
lore.content: The succession is contested by Princess Aurelie (blood), Lord Chancellor Vasse (law), and the Guilds' masked envoy (gold). Each holds a true claim and hides a true crime.

lore.title: The Whisper-Market
lore.content: Ashglance's unofficial exchange where secrets are bought, sold, and shorted like grain. The first stop for anyone who wants to know who really lit the fire.

lore.title: The Veil
lore.content: An order of masked envoys who broker between the Guilds and the Court. To remove a Veil's mask uninvited is a capital insult.

lore.title: The Ash-Saints
lore.content: Ashglance venerates ancestors whose ashes line the Sovereign's crypt. Some say the burned Sovereign has not yet joined them — and walks.

lore.title: The Writ of Succession
lore.content: The legal instrument that names the next Sovereign. Whoever holds the signed writ at the fortnight's end is crowned — and it has gone missing.

npcs.name: Steward Ysolde
npcs.description: The late Sovereign's steward, who knows where every body and ledger is buried.
npcs.personality: Discreet, precise, mordantly funny in private.
npcs.motivation: To see a worthy claimant crowned and the murderer named — in that order.

npcs.name: Princess Aurelie
npcs.description: The Sovereign's grieving daughter, claimant by blood.
npcs.personality: Composed, idealistic, hiding a ruinous debt.
npcs.motivation: To honor her father's reforms — and bury the debt that could be read as motive.

npcs.name: Lord Chancellor Vasse
npcs.description: The unburnt Chancellor, claimant by law.
npcs.personality: Urbane, paternal, never raises his voice.
npcs.motivation: To preserve the realm's order — and the inconvenient truth that he was first to the fire.

npcs.name: The Masked Envoy
npcs.description: The Guilds' Veil-envoy, claimant by gold.
npcs.personality: Courteous, unreadable, speaks in favors owed.
npcs.motivation: To install a Sovereign the Guilds can bill — and to keep the mask on.

npcs.name: Quill
npcs.description: A whisper-market broker who trades in everyone's secrets, including yours.
npcs.personality: Cheerful, amoral, scrupulously honest about prices.
npcs.motivation: Profit, and the long game of owing favors to the eventual winner.

npcs.name: Cinder
npcs.description: A Veil-trained killer the losing faction will eventually hire.
npcs.motivation: To remove whichever claimant their employer cannot out-argue.

adventures.title: Crown or Break a Claimant
adventures.premise: A burned throne, three claimants each with a true claim and a hidden crime, a missing writ of succession, and a fortnight to decide who rules Ashglance.
adventures.hook: A dead Sovereign's steward hires the party to recover the missing Writ of Succession and learn who lit the throne-fire.
adventures.villain: Whichever claimant set the fire — and the Veil-killer Cinder, who tidies the board for the losers.
adventures.setting: The smoke-stained Ivory Court, the Whisper-Market, the ash-crypt of Sovereigns, and the salons of three factions.
adventures.playerStakes: Back the wrong claimant and the city tips into purges and street-war; expose the wrong secret and the party becomes the next thing to be tidied away.
adventures.encounters: A whisper-market bidding war for a secret; a salon poisoning that must be prevented socially; the ash-crypt and its restless Sovereign; Cinder's strike on the party's chosen claimant.
adventures.climax: At the Court's final session the party must produce the Writ, name the fire-setter with proof the Court will accept, and survive Cinder's last attempt — then crown a Sovereign or break the line entirely.
adventures.resolution: Ashglance is crowned under a flawed but legitimate Sovereign, falls to a strongman, or abolishes the throne for a council — and the party's secrets are either currency or a noose for years to come.

quests.name: The Missing Writ
quests.description: Recover the Writ of Succession and name who lit the throne-fire before the fortnight ends — then crown or break a claimant.
objectives: Choose (or play) among the three claimants
Trace the Writ through the Whisper-Market
Prove who set the throne-fire to the Court's satisfaction
Survive the final session and decide the succession

quests.name: A Secret Worth a Crown
quests.description: Win the whisper-market bidding war for the secret that names the fire-setter.
objectives: Out-bid or out-trade a rival faction

quests.name: The Tidying
quests.description: Keep Cinder from removing your chosen claimant.
objectives: Identify Cinder's next mark from the salon gossip
Foil the assassination without open bloodshed

entries.text: A salon invitation arrives — and so does a rival, smiling.
Quill has a secret to sell that touches one of the party directly.
A faction offers a favor now for a vote later; refusing has a price too.
A street near the palace is suddenly, conspicuously empty.
Cinder is glimpsed leaving a room someone important was just in.
Faction thugs guarding a tomb they have no business in.
A cold draft and a shadow that wears a courtier's shape.
The burned Sovereign's specter, asking who let the fire in.
Cinder, cornered, offering a deal instead of a blade.
The Writ of Succession — and whoever else came for it tonight.
